hero.label: Made for Corgi Insurance
hero.headline: I want to be the first call Corgi's new product line ever makes.
hero.subheadline: Corgi is doing something genuinely rare: cutting out the carrier middleman so startups can get real insurance coverage without the usual months of back-and-forth. That full-stack model means a founding BDR here is selling something that actually works differently, not just priced differently. I want to be the person who figures out how to tell that story at scale.

whyCompany.title: Full-stack underwriting changes the entire sales conversation
whyCompany.body: Most insurance brokers are reselling someone else's risk appetite, which puts a ceiling on what they can promise a prospect. Because Corgi underwrites and issues policies directly, a BDR here can make commitments that brokers simply cannot match. That is a genuinely differentiated value proposition to open cold calls with, and I know how to use structural advantages like that.

whyCompany.title: Founding BDR at a new product line is a once-in-a-career timing play
whyCompany.body: There is no existing pipeline, no inherited playbook, and no one who has already figured out the ICP. That is exactly the kind of blank-canvas moment where someone who can move fast and iterate on messaging creates outsized impact. I am at the stage of my career where I want to build something, not inherit it.

whyCompany.title: I have already done this exact job in a fast-moving B2B context
whyCompany.body: At Copygen.ai I ran cold outreach end-to-end through HubSpot and LinkedIn sequences and contributed directly to signing 15 to 20 paying clients from scratch. At NextAfter I learned how B2B buyers in specialized industries respond to digital touchpoints and what messaging actually converts. The Corgi BDR role is the intersection of those two experiences.

quote: Insurance for startups is broken in a specific, fixable way, and Corgi has the architecture to actually fix it. I want to be the person on the front lines explaining that to founders before anyone else does.
